# Westword

> > Denver's alternative weekly covering investigative journalism, restaurant reviews, music profiles, and cultural criticism since the 1970s.

Westword is Denver's premier alternative newspaper, known for hard-hitting local investigations into municipal politics, corruption, and social issues, alongside comprehensive coverage of the city's dining scene, music culture, and arts. The publication features writers like Kyle Wagner, Michael Roberts, Steve Jackson, and Karen Bowers covering everything from Denver International Airport controversies to punk rock interviews.

## Key Topics

- Denver politics and municipal corruption
- Denver International Airport (DIA)
- Restaurant reviews and Denver dining
- Wellington Webb administration
- Pay-to-play politics and campaign finance
- Music scene and band profiles
- Film criticism and cult cinema
- John Waters and dark comedy
- Colorado social issues
- Investigative journalism
- Local government accountability
- Denver food culture
- Alternative weekly journalism
- Cultural criticism

## Investigative News & Politics

- [HATE SPRINGS ETERNAL](https://www.westword.com/news/hate-springs-eternal-5053999): Racist flier controversy in Colorado Springs amid Amendment 2 debate
- [CRASH AND CARRY](https://www.westword.com/news/crash-and-carry-5053648): Denver International Airport's troubled automated baggage system failures
- [BASE BEHAVIOR](https://www.westword.com/news/base-behavior-5053887): Investigation into National Guard misconduct and travel abuse (part 2)
- [GIVE UNTIL IT HURTS](https://www.westword.com/news/give-until-it-hurts-5053827): Investigation into pay-to-play politics with Denver Mayor Wellington Webb
- [ILL WILL](https://www.westword.com/news/ill-will-5053778): Lance Clem's wrongful termination lawsuit against Governor's AIDS Council
- [FILING A COSTLY FLIGHT PLAN](https://www.westword.com/news/filing-a-costly-flight-plan-5053763): Denver pays $14/word for overpriced Stapleton Airport consultant report
- [SCHOOL'S OUT](https://www.westword.com/news/schools-out-5053706): Former Auraria residents lose fight for education funding after displacement
- [WHAT RHYMES WITH "JERKWATER"?](https://www.westword.com/news/what-rhymes-with-jerkwater-5053647): Story of wrongful shoplifting conviction in Edgewater, Colorado
- [DIALING FOR DOLORS](https://www.westword.com/news/dialing-for-dolors-5053998): Controversy over NOAH food bank telemarketing fundraising on Capitol Hill

## Food & Restaurant Reviews

- [CADDY SHOCK](https://www.westword.com/food-drink/caddy-shock-5053838): Critical restaurant review of Cadillac Ranch at Larimer Square
- [MOUTHING OFF](https://www.westword.com/food-drink/mouthing-off-5054013): Brunch reviews comparing Le Central, Firefly Cafe, and City Spirit Cafe
- [LOCAL GYRO](https://www.westword.com/food-drink/local-gyro-5053883): Review of Yanni's Greek restaurant exploring traditional Mediterranean cuisine
- [THAI SOCIETY](https://www.westword.com/food-drink/thai-society-5053816): History and review of Thai restaurants in Denver since 1961
- [DIVE! DIVE!](https://www.westword.com/food-drink/dive-dive-5054080): Burger review at Skyline Cafe and Denver dive bars

## Music & Artist Profiles

- [GRAND OLD PUNKERS](https://www.westword.com/music/grand-old-punkers-5053791): Interview with Johnny Ramone on politics and punk rock conservatism
- [TALKIN' 'BOUT A REVOLUTION](https://www.westword.com/music/talkin-bout-a-revolution-5053944): Profile of poet Nikki Giovanni and the Black Arts Movement's jazz influence
- [THE KITTENS' MEOW](https://www.westword.com/music/the-kittens-meow-5053770): Profile of Chainsaw Kittens and frontman Tyson Meade from Oklahoma

## Arts & Film Criticism

- [JUNE WITH A CLEAVER](https://www.westword.com/arts-culture/june-with-a-cleaver-5053907): Film review of John Waters' Serial Mom, examining his evolution from cult cinema
- [OUT OF THE NORM](https://www.westword.com/news/out-of-the-norm-5054062): Profile of conservative radio host Norm Resnick and conspiracy theories

## Optional

- [LETTERS](https://www.westword.com/news/letters-5053725): Reader letters responding to Dennis Powell article and other issues
